CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow up of chronic problems.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Anna is a 44-year-old female with a past medical history significant for arthritis, gout, and reflux presenting for follow up of her chronic problems. She reports improvement in her arthritis, noting that she has been doing pilates and lifting weights which has helped build muscle and reduce joint pain. She has completed physical therapy for her right knee with good results and is now able to walk about a mile to a mile and a half per day. Regarding her gout, she had an episode of her right first big toe approximately two months ago which resolved with medication. She is currently taking allopurinol with no issues and denies further flare ups. For her reflux, she was placed on omeprazole and started dietary modifications, though she notes she has not completely eliminated certain foods yet. She continues to have episodes of nausea and vomiting in the mornings with actual vomiting, not just reflux. She also endorses abdominal pain and bloating. Her last bowel movement was two days ago and was normal without blood. She denies weight loss, fever, or chills.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for nausea, vomiting in the mornings, abdominal pain, and bloating. Negative for diarrhea, weight loss, fever, and chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Arthritis, gout, reflux.

MEDICATIONS
Omeprazole, allopurinol 100 milligrams once daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs are good. Heart sounds normal. Lungs sound normal. Abdominal examination reveals pain to the right upper quadrant on palpation with no rebound or guarding and no peritoneal signs. Right knee shows slight effusion with some pain to palpation and decreased range of motion.

RESULTS
Autoimmune panel is normal. Right knee x-ray shows no fracture but does demonstrate residual arthritis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Reflux, nausea, and vomiting: Order right upper quadrant ultrasound to rule out gallstones. Check labs. Continue omeprazole 40 milligrams once daily. Continue dietary modifications.
2. Gout: Well controlled. Continue allopurinol 100 milligrams once daily. Refill ordered.
3. Arthritis: Very pleased with progress of right knee. Continue pilates and using the knee. Follow up regarding any issues and discuss further imaging or intervention as needed.
